north_star_metric.name: Community Contribution Index
north_star_metric.definition: % of residents who have taken at least one community action per month (posted event, answered question, endorsed business, shared resource)
north_star_metric.why: Measures platform health as 'residents helping residents,' not vanity metrics like downloads or DAU
north_star_metric.aligned_with_nlros: Solves Cold Start Paradox + Influencer Monopoly by measuring diverse contribution, not engagement concentration

onboarding.problem: New user sees empty directory. No reason to invite friends.
onboarding.hypothesis: If we pre-populate with curated businesses + seed with block clubs, new users see a 'living' directory

experiment.name: Founder Pod Onboarding
experiment.variant_b: Sign-up → assigned to 'Pod' (cohort) with other new residents → shared challenges
experiment.metric: % who complete profile + invite 3+ friends within 7 days

business_adoption.problem: Business owners hesitate to list/post. 'Why should I trust this app?'
business_adoption.hypothesis: If we show 5 verified community members vouching for the platform, trust increases

experiment.name: Community Vouching Protocol
experiment.variant_b: Form + 'community members who vouched for us' section + transparent data policy
experiment.metric: Business account creation → first post within 2 weeks

resident_engagement.problem: Users sign up, post once, never return. App fatigue.
resident_engagement.hypothesis: If we create a weekly ritual (block update digest), users return habitually

experiment.name: Weekly Block Digest
experiment.variant_b: Thursday 6pm: 'What happened on your block this week' email + app push

referral_activation.problem: No mechanism for users to invite friends. Referrals are 0.
referral_activation.hypothesis: If users get 'founder' status for every 3 friends invited, they'll share

experiment.name: Founder Badge Referral Loop
experiment.variant_b: Invite 3+ friends → 'Founder' badge + 1 month free premium + featured on community board
experiment.metric: Invites per resident + referral conversion rate

trust_paradox.problem: Residents fear data harvesting. 'What data does this app collect?'
trust_paradox.hypothesis: If we publish exact data policy + monthly transparency report, concerns drop 60%

experiment.name: Radical Transparency Dashboard
experiment.variant_b: Public data audit dashboard: 'Here's everything we collect & why' + zero dark patterns badge

gentrification_resistance.problem: Platform could become tool for speculators. 'This will price out low-income residents.'
gentrification_resistance.hypothesis: If we offer 'Community First' pricing tier + pledge revenue to neighborhood fund, skepticism drops

experiment.name: Community First Tier
experiment.variant_b: Tier 1: Community-owned businesses (20% off) + revenue shared with neighborhood fund
experiment.metric: Adoption by local nonprofits + affordability perception survey

feature_virality.problem: No feature that residents naturally share. Growth is only via direct invites.
feature_virality.hypothesis: If we create a 'Weekly Block Alert' feature (emergency info, events, local updates), residents share it organically

experiment.name: Viral Block Alert System
experiment.variant_b: Quick-share block alerts: 'Street closed,' 'Lost pet,' 'Community meeting'
experiment.metric: Shares per alert + invite rate from alert page

dark_pattern_avoidance.problem: Temptation to use manipulative tactics for growth. NLROS warns against this.
dark_pattern_avoidance.hypothesis: If we design for trust + transparency first, growth is slower but sustainable

experiment.name: Ethical Growth Audit
experiment.variant_b: Monthly review: 'Did we use any dark patterns?' + publish results

property_manager_retention.problem: Property managers (long-term residents) aren't engaged. They could be huge retention lever.
property_manager_retention.hypothesis: If we create PM dashboard (tenant requests, maintenance tickets), they'll use platform weekly

experiment.name: Property Manager Dashboard
experiment.variant_b: Dashboard: tenant requests, maintenance coordination, lease management
experiment.metric: PM monthly active users + feature adoption

competitor_resilience.problem: When Meta launches 'Hyde Park Connect,' what's our unfair advantage?
competitor_resilience.hypothesis: If we're 'community-owned' + transparent, we survive Big Tech competition

experiment.name: Community Ownership Positioning
experiment.variant_b: Messaging: 'Built by Hyde Park residents, for Hyde Park' + community board seat
experiment.metric: Brand perception vs competitors + long-term retention

stages: New resident signs up → assigned to Pod (cohort)
Pod completes weekly challenge (e.g., 'find 3 local events,' 'endorse 1 business')
Contributions visible to block → triggers invites from neighbors
More invites → pod grows → bigger challenges → more contributions
Loop closes when resident becomes 'elder' and helps onboard next cohort
growth_loops.nlros_alignment: Solves Cold Start Paradox + Youth Exodus (long-term identity)

stages: Resident worries about data privacy
Sees public data audit dashboard
Reads transparent policy + monthly report
Invites skeptical friend ('it's actually trustworthy')
New resident immediately sees trust indicators → onboards faster
growth_loops.nlros_alignment: Solves Trust Breach + Surveillance Creep risks

stages: Business owner worries: 'Will anyone use this?'
Sees 5 resident testimonials + featured section
Posts first event → gets 10 RSVPs
Success → posts again → gets 20 RSVPs
Encourages other businesses → platform becomes essential
growth_loops.nlros_alignment: Solves Competitor Blitzkrieg (defensibility through business partnerships)

stages: Low-income residents worry: 'This will gentrify my neighborhood'
See 'Community First' tier (20% discount for nonprofits + co-ops)
See revenue share commitment (20% to neighborhood fund)
Build trust → contribute content → invite others
Neighborhood becomes more tightly knit → resists gentrification pressure

experimentation_cadence.decision_rule: If metric improves 20%+, ship it. If flat, iterate or kill.
experimentation_cadence.tracking: Weekly growth meeting: Which experiments learned something? What's next?
experimentation_cadence.aligned_with_crazy_horse: High-velocity experimentation culture removes friction, finds 10X improvements

weekly_cadence.friday: Growth meeting: results + next week planning
weekly_cadence.sunday: Review week's Community Contribution Index + cohort health

how_to_use: Query the growth hacking notebook with: notebooklm ask '<friction_point>' to get tactics from the playbook
integration_with_nlros: Every experiment should be checked against NLROS scenarios. E.g., 'Founder Badge Referral' - does it avoid dark patterns? Does it risk Influencer Monopoly? Does it resist Weaponization?
